name: Chileab
overview: Chileab was a male member of the tribe of Judah and is uniquely identified as the second-born son of King David. He holds a distinct place in biblical genealogy as recorded in the Old Testament. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond his birth order and lineage.
namesAndTitles: This individual is known primarily by the name Chileab, as mentioned in 2 Samuel 3:3. He is also referred to as Daniel in 1 Chronicles 3:1, a name meaning 'G-d is my judge.' Neither name is indicated as being directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Chileab was the son of King David and Abigail, establishing him firmly within the royal family of Israel. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these immediate relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Chileab's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his position as the second-born son of King David, a key figure in Israel's history. While the Scriptures mention him by name, there is little recorded about his personal deeds or role, highlighting the importance of his lineage rather than individual achievements. His mention alongside David and Abigail underscores the royal lineage through which God's covenant promises were fulfilled.
